chapter: Starting out in New York and Chicago
title: Israel Crosby, Sid Catlett, guitarist Hurley Ramey and Okeh recordings
summary: Looking at a photo, Horace names bassist Israel Crosby (later with Fletcher), Sid Catlett in Fletcher's Grand Terrace band, and Hurley Ramey, his only guitarist, added for his Okeh and Columbia records such as 'Ginger Bell'.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: And I had a bass player with me -- you must remember the name, Israel Crosby.
Who Later went on into Fletcher's band, but he was my bass player.
In this picture, he looks like a baby.
That -- is that drummer Sid Catlett?
That sure looks like him. You bet.
And he was in Fletcher's band at the Grant Terrace in Chicago. I had a little guitarist named

Bobby Lessee from Brooklyn, New York. Now that was in Fletcher's band. I only had one guitarist with me during the time that I had a band. His name was Hurley Ramey -- a Chicago boy. I haven't seen him for years. that's He was the only guitar player I ever had, and the only reason that I got him was because when I recorded for Okeh, and Columbia, I had to have, you know, four pieces going all the time because I had to stand up sometime and direct, and I made a couple of original tunes -- one called "Ginger Bell," and I needed him real badly on the opening record. (inaudible). So he did so well that I kept him. The only one.
And this is while you were at Swingland?
And these people in this picture were with Fletcher.
At the Grant Terrace. Uh-huh. Great.
